---
title: Configuration
---

Copy the template and replace its `CHANGE_ME` values:

```sh
cp config.template.yaml config.yaml
uv run restic-backups --config config.yaml check-config
```

There is no default configuration path. Pass `--config` before the command, or
set it once for the current shell:

```sh
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG="$PWD/config.yaml"
uv run restic-backups check-config
```

To use an encrypted configuration, encrypt it with SOPS and enable decryption
with either `--sops` or `RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1`:

```sh
cp config.template.yaml config.sops.yaml
sops config.sops.yaml
uv run restic-backups --config config.sops.yaml --sops check-config

export RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG="$PWD/config.sops.yaml"
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1
```

The values of `id` fields are user-defined names. They only need to be unique
within their section; references in other sections must match them exactly.

## `credentials`

`credentials` contains reusable S3 authentication details. Backblaze application
key IDs and application keys use the same fields as AWS access keys.

```yaml
credentials:
  - id: b2-credentials
    access-key-id: "..."
    secret-access-key: "..."
```

One credential may be referenced by several stores.

## `restic-stores`

`restic-stores` describes each restic repository and links it to an entry in
`credentials` through `credentials-id`.

```yaml
restic-stores:
  - id: b2-store
    credentials-id: b2-credentials
    enabled: true
    endpoint: https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
    region: us-west-004
    bucket: example-bucket
    key_prefix: voice-memos
    password: "..."
```

All stores use restic's S3 backend. `endpoint` identifies the S3-compatible
service, `region` configures request signing, and `bucket` plus `key_prefix`
locate the repository. `password` encrypts the restic repository. Disabled
stores are ignored by commands and may retain `CHANGE_ME` placeholders. An
enabled store fails validation until its store values and credentials are
complete.

## `backups`

`backups` names the jobs shown by the CLI. Each job selects a repository by
matching `restic-store-id` to a `restic-stores.id` value.

```yaml
backups:
  - id: voice-memos
    restic-store-id: b2-store
```

Several backup jobs may share a restic store.

## Optional archive policy

AWS stores may add an `archive` policy. `storage-class` controls how new
objects are stored, and `restore` defines retrieval behavior for cold storage:

```yaml
credentials:
  - id: aws-credentials
    access-key-id: "..."
    secret-access-key: "..."

restic-stores:
  - id: aws-store
    credentials-id: aws-credentials
    enabled: false
    endpoint: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
    region: us-east-1
    bucket: example-bucket
    key_prefix: backups
    password: "..."
    archive:
      storage-class: GLACIER_IR
      restore: null
```

Omit `archive` to use the storage provider's default class.

Use `GLACIER_IR` for immediate restic access. It must not define a restore
policy:

```yaml
archive:
  storage-class: GLACIER_IR
  restore: null
```

Cold classes require an explicit retrieval policy:

```yaml
archive:
  storage-class: GLACIER
  restore:
    tier: Bulk
    days: 7
    timeout: 24h
```

`GLACIER` accepts `Standard`, `Bulk`, or `Expedited`; `DEEP_ARCHIVE` accepts
`Standard` or `Bulk`. Retrieval commands also require an acknowledgement:

```sh
ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1 uv run restic-backups generic run \
  --backup <backup-id> restore latest --target <dir>
```

Changing a storage class affects new objects only. Use a new `key_prefix`
rather than mixing storage policies in one repository.

## Validation rules

`check-config` also rejects duplicate IDs, unknown credential or store
references, missing S3 fields, and invalid Glacier retrieval tiers or
durations. Managed-data resolution separately rejects unsafe path components.
